newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Afghan Taleban said to take key town.
newsitem.headline: Afghan Taleban said to take key town.

text.p: Afghanistan's Taleban Islamic militia recaptured the strategic town of Jabal os-Siraj north of the capital Kabul from its opponents on Tuesday, a Pakistan-based Afghan news service said.
The Afghan Islamic Press (AIP) quoted its sources in the area as saying the town, on the main highway from Kabul to the north, fell to the Islamic militia about midday.
The Taleban captured 14 opposition soldiers and five of its own fighters were killed, AIP said. There was no immediate information about opposition casualties.

Earlier on Tuesday, a Taleban official at Pul-i-Khumri, in the northeastern province of Baghlan, said the militia had captured the town of Golbahar in the adjacent Kapisa province in a big offensive against opposition forces loyal to opposition leader Ahmad Shah Masood.

"This morning the Taleban launched a very wide offensive on Golbahar, clearing the area. We have also captured the rear of Jabal os-Siraj and Masood's forces are now surrounded there," Taleban Information Minister Amir Khan Mutaqi told reporters at Pul-i-Khumri.
